repo.description:
### Summary

Application responses carried no frame-control headers, so the authenticated NocoDB interface could be embedded in a page hosted on any other origin and used for clickjacking.

### Details

Neither an `X-Frame-Options` header nor a Content-Security-Policy `frame-ancestors` directive was emitted on any response. The served application shell is produced by `gui.middleware.ts`, which terminates the request before the global middleware chain runs, so the response that actually renders the authenticated interface carried no frame restriction; API responses from `global.middleware.ts` and from the on-prem variant carried none either. The application also drew no distinction between the routes that are deliberately embeddable - the shared-view and shared-base links offered as iframe snippets in the share dialog - and the rest of the interface, so nothing anywhere told a browser which origins were permitted to frame a signed-in session.

### Impact

A signed-in user who visits an attacker's page could have the NocoDB interface loaded transparently beneath attacker-controlled content and be induced into clicking through to actions in their own session - modifying or deleting records, changing sharing settings, or inviting a collaborator - while believing they were interacting with the attacker's page. No authentication is required to host the framing page; the only requirement is that the victim holds an active session.

### Credit

This issue was reported by [@kazisabu](https://github.com/kazisabu) and [@iamshafayat](https://github.com/iamshafayat).
repo.summary: Clickjacking via Missing Frame Control Headers
